subject: MSA / Order Form: allocation of IP defense and remediation + insurance offset request
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 10 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Acme MSA/OF — prep: indemnity allocation + insurance offset ask

Hey team,

FYI — procurement at Acme asked for a final pass on indemnity allocation before we circulate the order form to their legal. They are specifically pushing on:

- who controls defense for third-party IP claims (right to defend vs. obligation to cooperate),
- what remediation obligations look like (patches, takedown, replacement), and
- whether insurance proceeds should offset Redwood's obligations.

Acme is expecting a response this week. I think we should propose:

1) Right to defend for Redwood for 3P IP claims affecting our core model outputs, with mandatory cooperation and approval over settlements;
2) Customer remediation limited to commercially reasonable measures and capping direct remediation costs to the order form cap;
3) Explicit carve for customer-provided data (customer retains responsibility);
4) Insurance offset language: allow proceeds from applicable insurance to reduce Redwood's indemnity payment but not to expand customer's recovery.

Kimberly — can you draft two short alternative paragraphs (one conservative for legal, one commercial for sales) we can send to Acme counsel? Markus — please note any procurement-side scheduling constraints.

Thanks,
Hannah

Hannah Schmitt
Head of Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Evan Bernard <ebernard@andersonllp.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sara Liu <sara.liu@acmehealth.com>, procure@acmehealth.com
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme MSA/OF — prep: indemnity allocation + insurance offset ask

Hannah / Kimberly,

Thanks for the note. Attached is Acme's response to your earlier redline (see Acme_MSA_redline_v2.docx). Their counsel flagged three items:

- Acme wants affirmative control of defense when the claim relates to outputs delivered to their customers (they argue operational impact).
- They will accept a right-to-defend if Redwood guarantees a remediation plan and a SLA for remediation milestones.
- They will not agree to a blanket insurance offset that meaningfully reduces their ability to be made whole; they proposed language that allows insurance proceeds to be applied only after judgment or settlement but not to reduce timely remediation payments.

We have also included a short evidence checklist Acme expects if a third-party claim arises (third-party-claim-evidence-list.xlsx).

From a drafting perspective, Acme is open to a split-control approach: Redwood handles defense but Acme can step in if Redwood is not taking commercially reasonable steps or if there's a material conflict. They also want to preserve the ability to seek injunctive relief directly.

Please confirm whether Redwood can accept step-in rights for Acme under narrow conditions and whether you have a proposed SLA / remediation timeline we can attach.

Best,
Evan Bernard
Anderson LLP (outside counsel to Acme Health)

Attachment: Acme_MSA_redline_v2.docx (redline), third-party-claim-evidence-list.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Evan Bernard <ebernard@andersonllp.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>, Sara Liu <sara.liu@acmehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme MSA/OF — prep: indemnity allocation + insurance offset ask

Evan / Sara — thanks for the redline and the checklist. Quick responses below and two options attached as inline wording.

High-level position: Redwood is willing to give right-to-defend with limited step-in for Acme, plus a concrete remediation SLA. We are not willing to accept language that eliminates an insurance offset entirely — it's a key mitigation for Redwood's financial exposure. However, we're happy to agree that insurance proceeds cannot be used to delay remediation obligations.

Two short alternative paragraphs (pick one):

Conservative (legal):
"Redwood shall have the right and sole control to defend any third-party claim subject to Redwood's obligation to consult with Customer. Customer may assume control only if Redwood fails to prosecute or defend the claim diligently after 30 days' written notice, or if a conflict of interest arises. Redwood's indemnity obligations shall be reduced by any insurance proceeds actually received by Redwood that are attributable to the claim, provided that any remediation required under this Agreement shall be commenced within the remediation timeline set forth in the Order Form and shall not be delayed by the application of insurance proceeds."

Commercial (sales):
"Redwood will, at its expense, defend and resolve third-party claims alleging that Redwood's model outputs infringe intellectual property rights, with Customer's reasonable cooperation. If Redwood does not commence a remediation plan within 15 business days of written notice, Customer may effect reasonable remediation and Redwood will reimburse documented remediation costs up to the Order Form cap. Insurance proceeds that accrue to Redwood may be applied to Redwood's indemnity obligations after settlement or judgment, but shall not be used to delay or reduce Customer's right to timely remediation."

Attached are the two paragraph snippets as a simple doc for review. Markus — procurement may push for immediate step-in; we should be ready with a timeline (15/30 days).

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference
From: Evan Bernard <ebernard@andersonllp.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sara Liu <sara.liu@acmehealth.com>, procure@acmehealth.com
Date: Wed, 13 May 2026 14:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme MSA/OF — prep: indemnity allocation + insurance offset ask

Thanks Kimberly — that helps. Acme's in-house says the commercial paragraph is closer to acceptable, but they insist on a 15-business-day remediation commences timeline and a unilateral right to seek injunctive relief (i.e., they need to be able to go to court to stop distribution while remediation occurs). They also want the insurance offset clause clarified so proceeds can only be applied after settlement or judgment, not to contractually cap remediation reimbursements.

Suggested edits (we can integrate these into the doc you sent):
- Keep the 15-business-day remediation kick-off.
- Add a carve that allows Acme to seek injunctive relief despite assignment of defense.
- Clarify that insurance proceeds received by Redwood may be applied to indemnity payments after Redwood has paid settlement/judgment amounts and shall not retroactively reduce documented remediation payments made in good faith by Customer within the remediation timeline.

Evan
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: Evan Bernard <ebernard@andersonllp.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sara Liu <sara.liu@acmehealth.com>, procure@acmehealth.com, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 14 May 2026 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme MSA/OF — allocation of IP defense and remediation + insurance offset request

Appreciate the quick turn. Agreement on next steps:

- Kimberly will update the commercial paragraph to include the 15-business-day remediation commencement and explicit statement that insurance proceeds apply after settlement/judgment and do not delay remediation reimbursements.
- We'll add a narrowly tailored injunctive-relief carve for Acme (they can seek injunctive relief where immediate harm is likely and Redwood fails to act).
- Markus will confirm procurement scheduling and whether Acme requires the final redline by EOD Monday (we think yes).

I'll circulate the updated snippet and an accompanying short SLA (milestone dates, notification cadence, evidence packet required) for signature-ready insertion into the Order Form.

If procurement pushes hard on removing the insurance offset language entirely, escalate to me and I'll loop VP of Sales — we should have commercial flexibility only if it doesn't expose us to uncapped remediation risk.

Thanks everyone — sending draft later today.

Hannah
Head of Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference
